_comment: Open questions that are not rulings. Items in group 'copy' need Brian's printed copy and stay as read until he answers; the autopilot decides the rest (AUTOPILOT.md, Mission 4). tools/decisions_page.py merges these with every proposed rulings/R-nnn.md into build/decisions.html. Remove an item once its answer has landed.

items.title: Map E: which Delta channels are major rivers?
items.context: The Delta branches and canals are printed at a middle width. We disagree with the second database on 72 hexsides (38 major→minor, 34 minor→major). Another 62 rows are the Fayum lake shore, the Nile running through a hex, or a channel the second database puts on the next hexside. All are left as read.
options: My Terrain Key says which channels are major (see note)
Take the second database's classes for the 72 disputed hexsides

items.title: Hill bands: ridge or slope?
items.context: Map E recorded 42 hill bands on rough ground as ridge, because the band lies on both sides of the hexside (the extractor's ridge rule). Measured the same way, 9 of Map D's 16 open hill-band rows are ridges (D2408|D2508, D2531|D2631, D2532|D2631, D2631|D2632, D2729|D2829, D2811|D2812, D2827|D2928, D2828|D2829, D2812|D2912; D3115|D3214 borderline).
options: Two-sided bands are ridges: set Map D's 9 to match Map E
Bands are slopes: revert Map E's 42 to slope
My Terrain Key says something else (see note)

items.title: Blue railways: finished or unfinished in 1940?
items.context: #64 made the blue Matruh–Capuzzo–Tobruk line on Map C an unfinished railroad. The Benghazi–Barce line (Map A) and the coast line east of Matruh (Map D: Fuka, Baggush) are also blue on the scan but kept as railroad.
options: Blue means unfinished everywhere: make A and D match C
Blue is just print colour: all three are railroad

items.title: Which side is higher at C0323|C0423?
items.context: Our band-side convention says C0323 is higher; the second database says C0423, a rough hill ringed by hachures. If the database is right, the convention needs a second look at depressions.
options: C0423 is higher: revisit the convention
Can't tell from my copy either
